content:
On the eve of a major iPhone launch event, Apple just rolled out a new iOS 26.6.2 software update for the iPhone. Here's what's in the update.

iOS 26.6.2 fixes an issue that prevented software updates from being installed over a cellular network

Apple is expected to release iOS 27 in the near future, quite possibly next week.

However, ahead of this major release, Apple today pushed out the smaller iOS 26.6.2 update.

You can install iOS 26.6.2 on your iPhone via the Software Update screen in Settings.

Here is Apple's official update notes:

Given the bug fix introduced in iOS 26.6.2, releasing it at this point, so close to the expected iOS 27 launch date, makes perfect sense.

If iOS 26.6.1 had prevented users from installing iOS 27 over a cellular network, it would have been a major headache for Apple and its users next week.

But by rolling out this update now, the hope is that more iPhones will already have the necessary fix in place before attempting to install the much-anticipated iOS 27 update.

So this update isn't anything particularly noteworthy, but it is a timely one ahead of iOS 27 and its host of new features.

Alongside iOS 26.6.2, Apple has also released iPadOS 26.6.2 for iPad, which includes the same bug fix.

Have you installed iOS 26.6.2 yet? Have you noticed any other changes? Let us know in the comments.
